I want to build a simplified version of Tax Data Blueprint Studio as a dynamic canvas-based documentation tool. The goal is to reduce complexity and start with a clean, consistent card-based system instead of multiple diagram shapes. All elements on the canvas must use a unified rectangular card design with a header and content body. There should be no diamonds, cylinders, or multiple visual shapes at this stage. Every node should visually look similar (a clean modern rectangular card with a header), and differences between node types should be expressed through color and content structure rather than shape variation.

Each card must support two primary types: “Table” and “Logic Note.” When creating or editing a card, the user should be able to click an Edit button (top-right corner of the card) which opens a modal dialog. In the modal, the user selects the card type (Table or Logic Note). If the type is Table, the modal allows defining a list of column names (simple structured list input). These column names should then be displayed inside the card body as a vertical list. If the type is Logic Note (for example, a calculation explanation or rule description), the modal should allow structured text input (title, description, bullet points). The card body should render this structured logic text clearly. All cards must support Delete and Edit actions via top-right controls.

Cards should be dynamically resizable (either auto-size based on content or manually adjustable). They should support drag-and-drop positioning on the canvas. The canvas should support smooth pan and zoom interactions. Nodes can be connected by lines to represent relationships, but the system does not need to implement table joins or data execution. Edges are visual relationships only, and each edge may optionally store simple metadata such as a label or short mapping description.

The design aesthetic should follow a clean modern graph-editor style inspired by tools like React Flow and Notion: subtle grid background, soft shadows, minimal borders, neutral color palette, and consistent typography. Colors should be used to differentiate card types (for example, blue for tables, purple for logic notes, orange for report outputs), but all cards must retain the same structural layout (header + body).

The system must be metadata-driven internally. The entire canvas (nodes, their type, positions, content, connections, and view state) must be exportable and importable as a complete portable project. Excel must be supported as a transport format, meaning exporting to Excel and importing back into a new instance must fully reconstruct the same canvas, including layout positions, card types, column lists, logic content, and connections. The internal structure used for Excel serialization should preserve full fidelity of the project but is not required to follow a rigid predefined sheet structure.

This application is strictly a documentation and visualization tool. It must not attempt to become a full tax calculation engine. The focus is on structured modeling, visual clarity, portability, and extensibility while keeping the UI simple and consistent.

Please design the data model, UI interaction flow, import/export logic, and MVP feature scope for this simplified version.

The aesthetic will be modern, influenced by React Flow and Notion, incorporating grids and shadows. The data model is metadata-driven for export and import as JSON and Excel. The data model involves `nodes` and `edges` arrays. Components will include a `BlueprintNode`, `Canvas`, `Sidebar`, `EditorModal`, and `Toolbar`. Export/Import with Excel is complex, I'm thinking of using multiple sheets to store the graph.

I've been working on the application structure now. I'm building it from the ground up, starting with *index.html* and setting up the standard boilerplate, then defining the crucial data structures in *types.ts*. The main components will be in *App.tsx*, with the React Flow integration implemented in *components/Canvas.tsx*. I'm also planning custom components for *NodeCard.tsx*, *EditorModal.tsx*, and *Sidebar.tsx*. I'm looking at implementing the Excel conversion logic in *services/excelService.ts*.

My Excel mapping structure will include nodes with ID, type, and detailed attributes, and edges defining source-target connections.
